advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Update docs/review-policy.md's local-approximation guidance (around line 27) to name the new `make verify` target instead of, or alongside, the spelled-out `make lint && make typecheck && make test` sequence.
evidence: Makefile:461 (changed) adds `verify: lint typecheck test  ## THE PRE-PUSH GATE: lint + typecheck + the default suite`, giving the local-approximation-of-Verified sequence a canonical target name
AGENTS.md:34-35 (changed) frames `make verify` as `the locally checkable half of Verified` and the only local command by which one can say 'I verified this'

docs/review-policy.md:23-29 owns this concept: '`Verified` is more than three make targets ... You can locally _approximate_ it with `make lint && make typecheck && make test` ... treat it as the source, not the three make targets' — naming the sequence but not `make verify`
docs/review-policy.md:3-8 declares the page 'the authoritative document for what those votes mean ... how to respond to each' and the normative content owner for `Verified`
advisory.finding: docs/review-policy.md, the declared authoritative page for the meaning of the `Verified` vote and the local approximation of it, still names only the spelled-out sequence `make lint && make typecheck && make test` and does not mention the new canonical `make verify` target this change introduces as the named pre-push proxy for `Verified`.
scenarios: A contributor reads review-policy.md (the normative Verified page) to learn how to check locally before push and is pointed at the raw three-target sequence rather than the single `make verify` target the rest of the docs now standardize on.
advisory.suggested_fix: In docs/review-policy.md line 27-29, replace the reference to `make lint && make typecheck && make test` with `make verify` (noting it wraps lint + typecheck + the default suite), while keeping the caveat that the workflow file is the authoritative superset.

evidence: `subprocess.run(["git", "init", "-q", "."], cwd=repo, check=True)` — no env passed, unlike the sibling test which uses `subprocess_env(...)` (line 196)
ABSENCE: the new git subprocesses set no `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL`/`GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM`/`HOME` isolation, so `--exclude-standard` reads the ambient user's excludes
advisory.finding: The new hermetic test `test_a_written_but_unstaged_gate_file_is_already_visible` runs `git init`/`git add`/`git ls-files` via plain `subprocess.run` without an isolated git environment; because `_existing_paths` uses `--exclude-standard`, git honors the developer's global `core.excludesFile` / `$GIT_DIR` / ambient git env, so a global gitignore rule matching e.g. `check_unstaged.py` (or `check_*`) could exclude the file and make the assertion `"scripts/check_unstaged.py" in before_staging` fail on an otherwise-correct implementation.

evidence: tests/unit/test_predates_gate_guard_parity.py:140: docstring — 'Widening from tracked-only to tracked-plus-untracked can only turn a FALSE GREEN red'
advisory.finding: Widening `_existing_paths` to include `--others` (untracked, non-ignored files) makes `test_completeness_every_gate_step_is_guarded_or_marked`, when run against the real `_ROOT`, sensitive to the developer's untracked working-tree state: a stray untracked `scripts|tests|docs/*.py|.txt|.json` (or `.github/*.txt|.json`) file matching a workflow `run:` body can turn the check red independent of the change under review.
